    //==
    // # Derived row access over the IJagged interface
    //
    // Row arithmetic written once against `IJagged<T>`
    // (`collections.concepts.plato`) so no mesh or adjacency file re-derives
    // offset slicing. Interface-receiver form throughout, as in the sections above.
    //
    // `JaggedArray<T>` needs no projection here: its `Offsets` and `Values` fields
    // satisfy the interface surface directly, so a type that HOLDS one reaches the row
    // vocabulary through that field (`mesh.Faces.Row(f)`). The projections for the
    // domain types that implement IJagged over differently-named storage live beside
    // those types (`topology.library.plato`).

    //==
    // # IJagged<T>
    //
    // Accessors derived from the two obligations. Every row query is bounds-free
    // by construction: the caller supplies a row in [0, RowCount).

    // The number of rows: one fewer than the number of offset boundaries.
    RowCount(self: IJagged<$T>): Integer
        => self.Offsets.Count - 1;
